content.title: RED FLAG WARNING: Wiregrass under fire weather watch
content.text: DOTHAN, Ala. (WDHN) — A Red Flag Warning has been issued for parts of Southeast Alabama, including the Wiregrass, as dangerous wildfire conditions move into the region this weekend. The warning is in effect Saturday, March 28, from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. CDT (11 a.m. to 8 p.m. EDT) and replaces an earlier Fire Weather Watch. “Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly,” the National Weather Service (NWS) in Tallahassee said in a release. “Outdoor burning is strongly discouraged!” What is a Red Flag Warning? A Red Flag Warning, according to the NWS, is issued when the weather creates “unfavorable” conditions that risk fire danger. It usually includes warm temperatures, low humidity and strong winds within 24 hours. Red Flag Warnings are usually only issued during the spring and fall fire weather seasons. It is used to alert fire managers on federal lands that the conditions for wildfires have an increased risk. Developing risk this weekend According to the agency’s forecast, a dry frontal passage combined with strong winds and very low humidity is creating the ideal conditions for fires to ignite and spread quickly. Winds: Northeast at 15 to 20 mph, with gusts up to 30 mph Humidity: Dropping as low as 18% in the afternoon Affected Area: Southeast Alabama, Southwest Georgia and most of the Florida Panhandle Between high winds and low humidity, the risk of wildfires significantly increases, especially in dry grass, brush and woodland areas. Precautionary steps to take According to previous reports, the Alabama Forestry Commission will not be issuing any burn permits for Saturday, and burning without a permit could result in a Class B misdemeanor charge. The NWS is urging residents in the affected areas to take precautions, and offers the following advice: Avoid outdoor burning and be extremely careful with open flames Keep vehicles off dry grass if possible Avoid using outdoor equipment that causes sparks Have an emergency plan in place and ready to go “Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly,” the NWS said in a release. “Outdoor burning is strongly discouraged!”
